Torah LM2/110 is a three-sentence oral record with no explicit bechina language in the source text. The word 'בְּחִינַת' does not appear. There are no dataset entries (reference === 1110 is absent from torahData.js). The source text contains no set of 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language that could form an independent domain.

The Torah's conceptual structure is as simple as any teaching in the corpus: the Rebbe answers a single direct question about free choice (בחירה) with a single direct answer. The full argument is:

  (1) Free choice is real and simple — a person always has it in everything, at every moment.
  (2) Many people feel they have no free choice because they are habituated to their ways from youth.
  (3) But this feeling is a false perception — the truth is that they can always change.

This structure yields exactly two thematic groupings: the reality of freedom (Package 1: good) and the illusion of constraint (Package 2: evil). These are identified in torah_110_additions.json and cover the full scope of this Torah's content. No additional independent domain exists in the text.

This Torah is best understood as an extremely brief practical note — a direct teaching response preserved by a disciple — rather than a developed thematic exposition. It does not develop conceptual clusters of 3+ bechina-related terms and therefore produces no new package proposals. When the dataset is eventually populated for reference 1110, the expected edges would minimally be: בחירה ↔ רצון (bechina: free choice is expressed through and equivalent to functional will).
